item.text: Euractiv reports that the Irish Presidency dropped language on cross-border clinical trials from its Biotech Act draft. EU countries are split over how to help patients join trials abroad.
Euractiv reports that Laura Ballarín Cereza (S&D), rapporteur on the KIDS Act, expects backing for a ban for under-15s. She also wants age limits for risky AI systems.

Agence Europe reports that co-rapporteur Siegfried Mureşan called Costa's proposal unacceptable. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden said it is still too large, and France called it very disappointing.

MLex reports that Parliament's committee vote on the Industrial Accelerator Act is set for 1 December, with compromises on the main political questions not yet agreed. Anna Cavazzini said the EPP is engaging constructively.
MLex reports that IMCO's opinion on the Digital Omnibus recommends exempting cloud providers from some switching obligations for certain older contracts.

Agence Europe reports that the Irish Presidency submitted a fourth Industrial Accelerator Act compromise on 23 November, to be discussed in the working party on 27 November. Ministers are to hold a policy debate on 3 December.
Agence Europe reports that Parliament confirmed the ITRE mandate on the European Competitiveness Fund on 25 November by 386 votes to 252, with 23 abstentions, after a challenge led by the PfE group.

Agence Europe reports that own resources co-rapporteurs Danuše Nerudová and Sandra Gómez López welcomed the revenue side of Costa's negotiating box but said Parliament will not accept its spending cuts.
Agence Europe reports that the leaders of Poland, Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia called Costa's negotiating box unacceptable on 23 November and plan to coordinate on cohesion and CAP funding.
Agence Europe reports that Norbert Lins, Dario Nardella and Barry Cowen wrote to António Costa on 24 November asking for about €93bn more for the CAP than his negotiating box provides.

Agence Europe reports that rapporteurs and shadows on the omnibus pesticide rules found no compromise on 23 November. They are to meet again on 14 December; a joint AGRI-ENVI vote could follow in January or February 2027.
